item.vignette: A patient with hereditary angioedema receives a GalNAc-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide. Hepatocyte synthesis of plasma prekallikrein falls, and bradykinin generation during contact-system activation is reduced.
item.lead_in: Which molecular event most directly produces the decrease in prekallikrein?

options.A: RNase H1-mediated degradation of prekallikrein mRNA after antisense binding
options.B: Irreversible inhibition of plasma kallikrein catalytic activity
options.C: Neutralization of circulating bradykinin by a monoclonal antibody
options.D: CRISPR-mediated disruption of the KLKB1 gene
options.E: Competitive antagonism of the bradykinin B2 receptor

item.tested_construct: Antisense binding to prekallikrein mRNA with RNase H1-mediated degradation
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Donidalorsen is a GalNAc-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide directed against prekallikrein mRNA in hepatocytes. Hybridization to the target transcript promotes RNase H1-mediated degradation, reducing prekallikrein protein and downstream bradykinin generation.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. Donidalorsen binds prekallikrein mRNA and promotes RNase H1-mediated transcript degradation.
distractor_explanations.B: Direct catalytic kallikrein inhibition is a different strategy and does not explain reduced hepatic prekallikrein synthesis.
distractor_explanations.C: The drug does not neutralize bradykinin protein directly.
distractor_explanations.D: Donidalorsen does not edit the KLKB1 genomic sequence.
distractor_explanations.E: B2-receptor antagonism blocks bradykinin signaling but does not lower prekallikrein synthesis.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate antisense-mediated reduction of prekallikrein synthesis from enzyme inhibition, bradykinin neutralization, receptor antagonism, and gene editing.

item.vignette: A patient with metastatic melanoma has a tumor lesion resected. Immune cells from that tumor are expanded in culture, cryopreserved, and later infused back into the same patient after lymphodepletion.

options.C: Peripheral-blood T cells engineered with a CD19 CAR
options.D: Autologous hematopoietic stem cells with a tumor receptor

item.tested_construct: Ex vivo expansion and reinfusion of autologous tumor-derived T cells
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Lifileucel is a tumor-derived autologous T-cell immunotherapy manufactured from resected tumor tissue by expanding tumor-derived immune cells in culture for reinfusion into the same patient.

distractor_explanations.A: The product is autologous, not donor-derived.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Lifileucel is composed primarily of expanded autologous tumor-derived T cells.
distractor_explanations.C: It is not a CAR-engineered peripheral-blood T-cell product.
distractor_explanations.D: It is not a hematopoietic stem-cell gene therapy.
distractor_explanations.E: It is not a dendritic-cell vaccine.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish tumor-derived autologous T-cell expansion from other cellular immunotherapy platforms.

item.vignette: Autologous T cells from a patient with synovial sarcoma are genetically modified to express a receptor that recognizes MAGE-A4. Treatment requires both tumor MAGE-A4 expression and a compatible HLA-A*02 allele.
item.lead_in: Why is the HLA restriction necessary for this therapy?

options.A: The engineered receptor recognizes soluble MAGE-A4 only after binding beta-2 microglobulin
options.B: MAGE-A4 must be secreted and captured by B-cell surface immunoglobulin
options.C: The engineered T-cell receptor recognizes a MAGE-A4 peptide only when presented by a compatible HLA class I molecule
options.D: The therapy depends on Fc-mediated binding to HLA-A*02-positive tumor cells
options.E: HLA-A*02 directly activates CD28 independently of antigen recognition

item.tested_construct: TCR recognition of MAGE-A4 peptide presented by compatible HLA class I
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Afamitresgene autoleucel consists of autologous T cells genetically modified to express a MAGE-A4-specific T-cell receptor. TCR recognition is HLA restricted: the receptor binds a MAGE-A4-derived peptide presented by a compatible HLA-A*02 class I molecule, triggering T-cell activation and cytotoxicity.

distractor_explanations.A: T-cell receptors recognize peptide-MHC complexes rather than soluble antigen bound to beta-2 microglobulin alone.
distractor_explanations.B: B-cell immunoglobulin is not involved in the engineered TCR recognition step.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. The engineered TCR recognizes MAGE-A4 peptide in the context of a compatible HLA-A*02 class I molecule.
distractor_explanations.D: This is a TCR-engineered cellular therapy, not an Fc-mediated antibody mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: HLA-A*02 does not directly activate CD28 independently of antigen-specific TCR recognition.

explanation.educational_objective: Use peptide-MHC restriction to explain why a MAGE-A4-specific engineered TCR therapy requires a compatible HLA-A*02 allele.

item.vignette: A c-Met-overexpressing lung cancer cell binds telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv and internalizes the antibody-drug conjugate. Lysosomal processing releases its cytotoxic small-molecule payload.
item.lead_in: Which intracellular process is most directly disrupted by the released payload?

options.E: PARP-mediated repair of single-strand DNA breaks

item.tested_construct: MMAE-mediated disruption of the microtubule network after c-Met-directed internalization
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv is a c-Met-directed antibody-drug conjugate linked to monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE). After c-Met binding and internalization, released MMAE disrupts the microtubule network, causing cell-cycle arrest and cell death.

distractor_explanations.A: Topoisomerase I inhibition is the payload mechanism of other antibody-drug conjugates, not telisotuzumab vedotin.
distractor_explanations.B: The cytotoxic effect is not caused by proteasomal degradation of c-Met.
distractor_explanations.C: Ribosomal translocation is not the direct target of MMAE.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. MMAE inhibits microtubule polymerization and disrupts the microtubule network.
distractor_explanations.E: PARP inhibition is a distinct DNA-repair mechanism.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect vedotin/MMAE antibody-drug conjugates with intracellular microtubule disruption after target-mediated internalization.

item.vignette: Skeletal muscle mitochondria from a patient with Barth syndrome have abnormal inner-membrane architecture due to disordered cardiolipin remodeling. Elamipretide improves mitochondrial function without replacing tafazzin.
item.lead_in: Which mitochondrial component is directly bound by this drug?

options.E: Cardiolipin in the inner mitochondrial membrane

item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Elamipretide is a mitochondrial cardiolipin binder. Cardiolipin is enriched in the inner mitochondrial membrane and contributes to membrane architecture and organization of respiratory-chain proteins; binding cardiolipin is the established direct pharmacologic action of elamipretide.

distractor_explanations.A: Complex I is not the direct binding target of elamipretide.
distractor_explanations.B: The drug does not act by inhibiting or activating mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma.
distractor_explanations.C: Adenine nucleotide translocase participates in ADP/ATP exchange but is not the labeled direct target.
distractor_explanations.D: Cytochrome c oxidase is a respiratory-chain enzyme and is not the direct binding target.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Elamipretide directly binds cardiolipin in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize cardiolipin as an inner-mitochondrial-membrane target and distinguish direct membrane-lipid binding from respiratory-enzyme targets.
